title: Verb relations: synonyms, antonyms, transitive pairs and honorifics, with notes

rows: to go, to come, to be (honorific)
to be saved, to be helped
to be finished, to be settled
to be baked, to be burnt
to escape, to get away from
済む means a matter is settled or done (often with 〜なくて済む, 'no need to'); 終わる is the plain word for something ending.
召し上がる is the honorific form: use it for the other person's eating, never your own.
いただく is the humble form for your own eating or receiving; also said before a meal.
おっしゃる is the honorific form of 言う, used for what a superior says.
申す is the humble form of 言う, used for what you yourself say to a superior (申します).
いらっしゃる is the honorific of 行く, 来る and いる.
参る is the humble form of 行く and 来る (駅へ参ります).
伺う is the humble form for visiting a person or asking (明日伺います).
見える is a polite way to say a guest has come (お客様が見えました).
なさる is the honorific of する (何をなさいますか).
与える is the formal, abstract 'give' (影響を与える); あげる is for everyday giving to others.
やる is casual and used for giving to animals, plants and juniors; あげる is the neutral polite form.
くださる is the honorific of くれる: someone above you gives to you.
いただく is the humble of もらう (先生にいただきました).
尋ねる is more formal; 聞く is the plain word for asking a question or listening.
加える is formal and abstract (説明を加える); 足す is everyday adding of numbers and amounts.
越える crosses an obstacle or border (山を越える); 超える goes beyond a limit or number (百人を超える).
眠る is being asleep; 寝る is lying down or going to bed, and can mean going to sleep.
亡くなる is the polite, soft way to say someone has died.
勤める means being employed at a place (銀行に勤める); 働く is working in general.
招く is to invite a guest formally; 呼ぶ also covers calling someone over or calling a name.
招く is for hosting guests; 誘う is a casual invitation to do something together.
知らせる is to let someone know a fact or news; 伝える passes on a message or feeling.
並べる is to arrange things in a row; 並ぶ is to line up or stand in a row.
育てる is to raise a child or plant; 育つ is to grow up.
届ける is to deliver; 届く is to arrive or reach.
沸かす is to boil water; 沸く is for water to boil.
伸ばす is to stretch or grow something; 伸びる is to stretch or grow by itself.
戻す is to put something back; 戻る is to go back.
乗せる is to give someone a ride or load something; 乗る is to get on.
割る is to break something; 割れる is for it to break.
切る is to cut something; 切れる is to be cut or to run out.
焼く is to bake or grill; 焼ける is to be baked or burnt.
汚す is to make dirty; 汚れる is to get dirty.
倒す is to knock down; 倒れる is to fall down.
流す is to pour or flush; 流れる is to flow.
動かす is to move something; 動く is to move.
減らす is to reduce; 減る is to decrease.
冷やす is to cool something; 冷える is to get cold.
温める is to heat something; 温まる is to warm up.
助ける is to rescue; 助かる is to be saved (also: that helps).
乾かす is to dry something; 乾く is to get dry.
燃やす is to burn something; 燃える is to burn.
曲げる is to bend; 曲がる is to bend or to turn a corner.
見つける is to find on purpose; 見つかる is to be found.
入れる is to put in; 入る is to go in.
出す is to take out or send; 出る is to go out.
上げる is to raise; 上がる is to go up.
下げる is to lower; 下がる is to go down.
起こす is to wake someone or cause something; 起きる is to wake up or happen.
付ける is to attach or turn on; 付く is to be attached.
掛ける is to hang or make (a call); 掛かる is to hang, or to cost or take (time).
始める and 終える are done by someone; the by-itself pair is 始まる and 終わる.
Both happen by themselves: a class begins and ends.
Both change by themselves: the number goes up or down.
Both are done by someone: to increase or to reduce.
勝つ is to win; 負ける is to lose.
作る is to make; 壊す is to break.
建てる is to build; 壊す is to tear down.
付ける is to switch on a light or TV; 消す is to switch off or erase.
教える is to teach; 習う is to learn from a teacher.
送る is to send; 受け取る is to receive.
与える is to give; 奪う is to take away.
拾う is to pick up; 捨てる is to throw away.
取る is to take; 置く is to put down.
上がる is to go up; 下がる is to go down.
上げる is to raise; 下げる is to lower.
生まれる is to be born; 死ぬ is to die.
生きる is to live; 死ぬ is to die.
思い出す is to recall; 忘れる is to forget.
喜ぶ is to be glad; 悲しむ is to be sad.
近付く is to come near; 離れる is to move away.
結ぶ is to tie; 解く is to untie or solve.
続ける is to continue; やめる is to stop.
辞める is to quit a job or school; 続ける is to keep going.
乾く is to get dry; 濡れる is to get wet.
洗う is to wash; 汚す is to make dirty.
冷える is to get cold; 温まる is to warm up.
温める is to heat; 冷やす is to cool.
登る is to climb; 下りる is to come down.
閉じる is to close (eyes, a book); 開く is to open.
探す is the search; 見つける is the result of finding. You can search without finding.
探す looks for something concrete; 求める seeks or demands something abstract (仕事を求める).
直す fixes things and mistakes; 治す cures illness or injury.
Both are なおる: 治る is for illness, 直る is for things that get fixed or habits that change.
考える is to think something through; 思う is an opinion or feeling (〜と思います).
知る is to come to know a fact; 分かる is to understand.
覚える is to memorize or remember; 習う is to learn from someone.
述べる is formal: to state an opinion in speech or writing.
語る is to tell at length or with feeling, like a story.
Both are たずねる: 尋ねる is to ask, 訪ねる is to visit.
訪ねる is to visit a place or person; 会う is to meet.
計る measures time and amounts; 測る measures length, size and depth.
眺める is to look at a view from a distance; 見つめる is to stare intently.
示す shows or points out; 表す expresses a feeling or meaning.
認める is to admit or approve; 許す is to forgive or permit.
守る is to protect or keep a rule; 防ぐ is to prevent something from happening.
保つ is to keep a state going (健康を保つ); 守る is to protect or obey.
調べる is to look into something; 確かめる is to check that something is true.
逃れる is formal and often abstract (責任を逃れる).
着く is to arrive; 届く is for a thing to reach someone.
運ぶ is to carry things; 連れる is to take a person or animal along.
選ぶ is to pick from options; 決める is to make a decision.
遊ぶ is to play or hang out; 楽しむ is to enjoy something.
増える is for a number to rise; 加わる is to join or be added.
履く goes with shoes and trousers, 脱ぐ takes them off.
見る is to look on purpose; 見える is for something to be visible by itself.
